user: The grafana dashboard for queue depth is on the ops board.
We renamed the ingest topic to events.raw last quarter.
Backups run at 03:00 UTC into the cold bucket.
The linter config lives in pyproject under tool.ruff.
I usually review PRs in the morning before standup.
The staging cluster has three nodes, production has nine.
Our error budget for the quarter is 99.5 percent.
The feature flag service is called switchboard.
We use conventional commits across all repositories.
The oncall rotation is weekly, starting Mondays.
Log retention is thirty days in the hot tier.
The design doc template lives in docs/templates.
We deprecated the v1 endpoints but have not removed them.
The load test harness is written in Go.
My editor is configured with format-on-save.
The metrics pipeline batches every sixty seconds.
We moved issue tracking from Jira to Linear.
The cache eviction policy is least-recently-used.
There is a nightly job that prunes orphaned blobs.
The auth service issues tokens valid for one hour.
We keep architecture decisions in numbered ADR files.
The schema registry rejects backwards-incompatible changes.
Our docker base image is distroless.
The search index is rebuilt weekly on Sundays.
I take notes in plain markdown files, one per day.
The billing reconciliation runs on the first of the month.
We shard the write path by tenant id.
The retry policy is three attempts with jitter.
Secrets are mounted from the vault sidecar, never baked in.
The changelog is generated from commit subjects.
We run static analysis in a separate CI job.
The queue consumer prefetch is set to ten.
Our SLO dashboards refresh every five minutes.
The archive format we standardised on is zstd.
I prefer small pull requests over large ones.
The integration suite needs docker compose running.
We label flaky tests and quarantine them.
The API gateway terminates TLS at the edge.
Config changes require a second approver.
The data warehouse loads land in the staging schema first.
